posts.text: YC Startup School 2026! Huge opportunity that I am very grateful for, hyped to meet everyone there. :D If you're in SF and or attending SUS this summer, would love to connect and chat! P.S. If you need a referral drop a comment and I'll send the link!

Really happy to share that I've joined Althra as a Venture Scout, working alongside Sanket Mittal and the team! Althra is a Canadian startup accelerator backing ambitious founders at the early stages with a $12,500 initial investment and potential $50,000 follow-on, plus access to a network of venture fund partners. If you're a founder in Alberta building something generational or interested at all, please do not hesitate to hit me up! Would love to hear what you're working on.
In the land of opportunity (SF) for the second time in my life. If you're in the Bay Area, I would love to meet!

After finishing the bulk of my university applications, everything has felt strangely empty. Those applications felt like a reflection of who I am and everything I've worked toward, all compressed into a few pages. Now, everything is up to chance, and years of effort are out of my control. After some reflection, I realized it isn't just luck. Every essay, every activity, every grade came from the time and effort I chose to put in. Greatest present I could have asked for this christmas

Progress usually feels invisible. As the year comes to a close, I was cleaning out my GitHub repos and came across my very first website. Throughout my journey, it never felt like I was improving. Same bugs, same confusion, same late nights. But looking back, there’s clear improvement. Growth doesn’t usually show up day to day. It shows up when you pause and realize how far you’ve come. Keep building, even when it feels like nothing’s changing.

Recently, I've felt more lost than ever. Not necessarily because I don't know what I want to do, but because there is so much I want to do and learn. Low-level code, DSA, robotics, videography, writing, building things that don’t even exist yet. It’s overwhelming and scary in a strange way. Not a lack of direction, but an excess of it. I’m learning that feeling lost doesn’t always mean you’re behind. Sometimes it means you’ve finally zoomed out enough to see how big the world is.
Every time I face the slightest inconvenience, I think about building an AI B2C SaaS to solve it. I'm in my prime right now.
